title: Values and loops in Lua
summary: Use local values, a sequence table, and ipairs to count positives.

scenario.briefing: A game studio tallies positive score changes in Lua.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: The loop already visits every score.
Compare the current value with zero.
Use an if statement around the increment.
Add if value > 0 then count = count + 1 end inside the loop.

misconceptions.description: Assigning without local inside a function.
misconceptions.feedback: An undeclared assignment creates a global. Declare counters and helpers with local unless sharing is intentional.
ipairs stops at the first nil and ignores non-integer keys. Use pairs for a map and ipairs for a sequence.

sections.title: Local values and dynamic types
sections.body: A local declaration limits a name to the block where it appears. Lua values carry a type, but a variable is not locked to one: the same name can hold a number, a string, a boolean, or a table at different times.

sections.title: Tables hold sequences
sections.body: A table is Lua's compound value and can act as both an array and a map. The sequence { 3, -1, 2 } has keys 1, 2, and 3. ipairs walks consecutive integer keys starting at 1 and stops at the first nil.

sections.title: Loops and conditions
sections.body: A numeric or generic for loop repeats a body, and an if statement selects a branch. Indentation is cosmetic; the end keywords close the loop and the conditional.

steps.title: Count positive score changes
steps.prompt: Edit main.lua. count_positive returns how many values are greater than zero.

files.content:
local function count_positive(values)
  local count = 0
  for _, value in ipairs(values) do
    count = count + 0 -- TODO: count positive values
  end
  return count
end

print(count_positive({ 3, -1, 2 }))

tests.description: The function keeps the taught name and parameter.
The loop counts only values greater than zero.

steps.title: Values and loops

statements.label: A local name is visible only inside the block that declares it.
A Lua variable is locked to the type of its first value.
ipairs visits integer keys starting at 1 and stops at the first nil.
Lua table indexes start at zero.

steps.explanation: Lua is dynamically typed: a name can hold any value, and local controls scope rather than type. Tables are the single compound structure, sequences start at index 1, and ipairs follows that sequence until a nil.
